answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by vesting rewards over time instead of paying instantly. Each identity must lock a deposit and keep an auditable record for several epochs before its earnings unlock; a whisper of new accounts gains nothing at once. Like a lagoon that fills slowly, trust accumulates only through sustained honest work, and a sonnet of fake identities cannot shortcut the wait: splitting one deposit across many names only creates many small, slow-vesting claims, so mass forgery costs time and locked capital without multiplying income.
